newsitem.title: USA: US West "long-way" from Time Warner deal - analyst.
newsitem.headline: US West "long-way" from Time Warner deal - analyst.

text.p: U. S. West Media Group President and CEO Charles Lillis told analysts during a conference call on Thursday that the company was a "long way" from reaching an agreement over restructuring its partnership with Time Warner Inc, said an analyst listening in on the call.

The analyst said Lillis confirmed that the two companies have pursued talks agrressively and added that Time Warner's approach to negotiations was "aggressive" and US West has been "responsive." Lillis characterized the situation as "very complex" and declined further comment, the analyst said.
A spokesman for U.S. West Media confirmed the statements.
In response to a question, Lillis said the second quarter would be the very earliest "to expect anything to happen with the Time Warner deal", the spokesman added.

According to published reports, U.S. West is considering a plan which would involve acquiring some of Time Warner's cable subscribers in exchange for assuming a portion of Time Warner's debt and giving up its interest in Time Warner's film and television assets.

U.S. West Inc currently holds a 25.5 percent stake in a partnership with Time Warner. The Time Warner partnership holds cable assets with 9.9 million subscribers as well as 100 percent ownership of HBO and Warner Brothers Studios.
U.S. West Media is a unit of U.S. West Inc.
